square_approximation_clarification.finding: No mathematical obstruction found. The one-test full-limit argument for the original bump is justified by the finite-R argument, not by assuming that every smooth-square approximant has a full spectral limit.
square_approximation_clarification.explicit_argument: Let eta_j=||omega_j-omega||_infinity and fix R, then a small lower endpoint. Uniform compact spectral mass bounds give sup_s large |C_s(omega_j)-C_s(omega)| <= M eta_j. Apply the finite-R Stieltjes identity for omega_j, replace C(omega_j) by C(omega), and bound the replacement by M eta_j times [R k(R)+integral_0^R |y k'(y)|dy]. The positive variance mass bound also gives limsup |V(omega_j)-V(omega)| <= M' eta_j. Take T to infinity, then j to infinity at fixed R; finally remove the small endpoint and let R grow. For full equality use the already established positive tails, with midrange constants controlled by the common compact support and sup norms; fixed-j outer errors disappear before j varies.
